# Windows `.cmd` Wrapper Analysis

> **Story:** A.5 — Windows Wrapper & Cross-Platform Test Matrix
> **Gargalo:** G6 (Install UX Hardening audit, 2026-04-14)
> **Date:** 2026-04-15
> **Author:** @developer (Pixel)
> **Related:** `docs/epics/epic-install-ux-hardening.md`

## Question

Does the npm-auto-generated `.cmd` wrapper for the `sinapse` and `sinapse-ai` binaries work reliably on Windows across all supported package managers (npm, pnpm, yarn)? Do we need a custom wrapper?

## TL;DR

**No custom wrapper is needed.** npm's auto-generated `.cmd` + `.ps1` shims are sufficient for all three package managers provided two conditions are met, both of which this repo already satisfies:

1. Every file listed under `package.json#bin` starts with a valid shebang: `#!/usr/bin/env node`
2. The file has Unix line endings (`LF`), not CRLF, even on Windows

The real Windows risk is NOT the wrapper itself — it is node/npm pathing edge cases and agent-sync running at the wrong time. Those are addressed by Stories A.1 (postinstall) and A.3 (doctor exception classification), not by a custom wrapper.

## Investigation

### How npm generates the wrapper

When a package declares a `bin` field:

```json
"bin": {
  "sinapse": "bin/sinapse.js",
  "sinapse-ai": "bin/cli.js"
}
```

npm's install process invokes `node-gyp`/`cmd-shim` to create three files per entry point inside the install prefix's `node_modules/.bin/` (or global `npm bin`):

| File | Used by |
|------|---------|
| `sinapse` | Unix shells (bash, zsh, fish) |
| `sinapse.cmd` | Windows `cmd.exe` |
| `sinapse.ps1` | PowerShell / pwsh |

The `.cmd` file is a simple batch script that locates `node.exe` on PATH and invokes it against the target `.js` file, forwarding all arguments. It is NOT fragile in practice as long as the shebang is respected as a marker and line endings are LF.

### What the audit (2026-04-14) actually flagged

The G6 entry in the audit says "Windows `.cmd` wrapper fragility". Re-reading the evidence, the audit's concrete symptom was:

> On Windows, `sinapse` sometimes fails to resolve immediately after `npm install -g`.

But the root cause turned out to be:

1. Fresh global install completes, `.cmd` is written correctly
2. Claude Code does NOT yet have the agents at `.claude/commands/SINAPSE/agents/`
3. User invokes `@developer`, it fails — and the user blames the install
4. Story A.1 (postinstall) copies agents automatically — fixing this for real

The `.cmd` itself was never broken in any of the samples the audit collected. The symptom was misattributed.

### Package manager differences

| PM | Wrapper behavior | Notes |
|----|-----------------|-------|
| npm | Generates `.cmd` + `.ps1` via `cmd-shim` | Baseline. Works on Windows 10/11 with Node >= 18. |
| pnpm | Generates `.cmd` via its own shim | Compatible; installs to `~/.local/share/pnpm` on Linux/macOS and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pnpm` on Windows. User needs `pnpm setup` once to add to PATH. |
| yarn | Classic generates `.cmd`; Berry uses PnP | Classic (v1) works identically to npm. Berry (v2+) runs via `yarn sinapse` or `yarn dlx`, no global `.cmd`. |

**All three** rely on the same shebang + LF conventions. If npm's wrapper works, theirs do too.

### Line ending check

```text
$ file bin/sinapse.js bin/cli.js
bin/sinapse.js: a /usr/bin/env node script, ASCII text executable
bin/cli.js:     a /usr/bin/env node script, ASCII text executable
```

Both have shebang `#!/usr/bin/env node`. Repo `.gitattributes` enforces LF for `*.js`. No action needed.

### Known edge cases and their mitigations

| Edge case | Mitigation |
|-----------|-----------|
| User's Node.js install is not on PATH | Doctor check `node-version` already reports this (A.3 keeps it as `fail`). |
| `pnpm setup` never run | Documented in installation docs; fresh `pnpm add -g` flow tested in the matrix. |
| Global install as administrator on Windows writes wrapper to a path non-admin shell can't see | Documented workaround: re-install as current user, or use `npx sinapse-ai`. |
| Yarn Berry (PnP mode) | Users use `yarn dlx sinapse-ai` instead; covered in matrix. |
| Symlink issues on network drives | Out of scope — neither npm nor a custom wrapper fixes this. |
| CRLF line endings introduced by `git config core.autocrlf=true` in a user clone | Tests can detect via `file bin/sinapse.js`. Not triggered by npm installs (which pull tarballs, not git). |

## Decision

**Keep the status quo — no custom `.cmd` wrapper.**

Reasons:

1. The npm auto-generated shim is the universal convention; departing from it adds maintenance burden and breaks with future npm/pnpm/yarn changes.
2. Every "wrapper failure" reported in the audit traces to A.1/A.2/A.3 root causes, not to the shim itself.
3. A custom wrapper would have to be generated by our own postinstall script, duplicating work that npm already does and opening new failure modes (stale shim after upgrade, permission issues, etc.).
4. Cross-platform test matrix (Story A.5, next section of this file family) validates the shim on the 27-combo grid on every release PR.

## Required safeguards (retained)

Even though we do not ship a custom wrapper, these are the things that MUST remain true for the shim to work reliably:

- [ ] `bin/sinapse.js` and `bin/cli.js` start with `#!/usr/bin/env node` (validated by `validate:publish` script)
- [ ] Both files have Unix (`LF`) line endings (enforced by `.gitattributes`)
- [ ] `package.json#bin` paths match the real files (validated by `validate:manifest` script)
- [ ] `postinstall` from Story A.1 runs `sync:ide` so agents are present when the shim is first invoked
- [ ] `doctor` from Story A.3 does NOT mark missing PATH as `fail` for pnpm/yarn cases where `dlx`/`npx` is acceptable

## Follow-up

No follow-up story required. Re-evaluate if a future release sees a non-trivial failure rate specifically attributable to the wrapper (not misattributed, like the A.1 symptoms were).
